newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Lubumbashi people jovial at Zaire rebel takeover.
newsitem.headline: Lubumbashi people jovial at Zaire rebel takeover.

text.p: The sound of renewed heavy fighting echoed across Zaire's second city on Thursday -- the morning after rebels took control of the economic backbone of the troubled Central African country.
Gunshots and artillery blasts were heard from the direction of the airport, about six km (four miles) northeast of the city and it was not clear who was in control of the airfield.
Sporadic machinegun fire also rang out from other parts of Lubumbashi and a pall of black smoke billowed into the sky from the blazing villa of President Mobutu Sese Seko.
Witnesses said huge crowds of civilians had stripped the residence on the southern edge of town before torching it.
Residents jubilant at the arrival of Laurent Kabila's rebels also pulled down posters of the president and burnt them in the streets.
The city of a million people was calm overnight after heavy firing near the airport. Two planes were heard flying out late in the evening with their lights off, but no one could say who was on them.
Before dawn noisy crowds arrived at army fields near the city's abandoned military headquarters and began stripping them of all the maize growing there.
Civilians had already stripped the former army headquarters of food and anything they could carry - cupboards, carpets, and chairs. Abandoned rocket launchers lay scattered at the base.
"We want Kabila to come and free us. We have no work and no food," said Moise Mwinkeyu, carting away sacks of maize on an old black bicycle.
Some people came across a small lake by canoe to join in the festive looting of the fields in the south of the city.
Residents there said homeless children had begun looting shops in the city centre in the night, joined by adults with guns, some said to be deserting soldiers in mufti.
"The forces of Kabila came and restored some order, it is largely calm now," a resident at the central Park Hotel said on Thursday morning.
Kabila's rebels, wearing dark olive fatigues, black berets and boots, entered the city from the direction of the Zambian border on Wednesday and government forces fled before them.

The rebels said they met fierce resistance some 15 km (10 miles) out of town, after which they had marched in. One commander said he had two wounded men. There had been heavy mortar and gunfire through the early afternoon.
Kabila's Alliance of Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire now controls about half of the country, including all major major cities but the capital Kinshasa, 1,800 km (1,100 miles) away.
